plain_summary: This page defines the responsible party for Cargo Dues, stating that it is payable by the importer/exporter, who may appoint an agent. It specifies that if Cargo Dues Orders are not received, charges will be billed to the container operator per TEU for container traffic and to the vessel agent for bulk and break-bulk traffic. It also details the billing for uncleared containers and LCL consignments. The page then introduces 'Late Order Fees' for late submission of Cargo Dues Orders, defining what constitutes a late submission and how interest is calculated. An example calculation for late order fees is provided, along with an exception for public holidays and weekends. Finally, it mentions incremental late order fees for non-submission, with further details expected on a subsequent page.

formulas.formula_as_written: Interest = Value of Order * (Prime Rate + 1%) * (Number of days late / 365)
formulas.what_it_calculates: Interest charged on late submission of Cargo Dues Orders.
formulas.units: South African Rand (R) for Value of Order and Interest, percentage for Prime Rate, days for Number of days late.
formulas.rounding_or_conditions: The first public holiday and first weekend will be excluded if they fall within the number of days that the Order has been submitted late for purposes of interest calculation. Example shows interest rounded to 2 decimal places.
